what: Venezuela signs deal with US energy giant to rebuild power grid

clean_source_blocks.text: Venezuela's interim president has signed an agreement with US energy giant General Electric to rebuild the country's electricity grid. Delcy Rodríguez, who was sworn in shortly after US forces seized Venezuela's leader, Nicolás Maduro, in January, announced the move at a televised event at the presidential palace on Monday. The agreement is the latest sign that the interim leader - who was a fierce critic of the US before Maduro's ouster - is opening up Venezuela's economy to US investors and companies. Critics of her government have warned that while Rodríguez appears to be loosening the state's control over the economy, many key institutions remain firmly under her party's control. Venezuela suffers from frequent power cuts and its power system - which was nationalised in 2007 under Maduro's mentor, Hugo Chávez - is in dire need of repair and investment.
The deal with General Electric is the latest sign of co-operation between US firms and Venezuela's interim government.

Venezuela signed an agreement on Monday, June 15, with General Electric for the US utility giant to rebuild its decrepit power grid, the South American country's interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, said. Most of Venezuela, including the capital Caracas, endures daily blackouts lasting up to 10 hours as the country deals with decades of neglect and underinvestment in the energy sector and elsewhere. Speaking alongside GE executives at the presidential palace, Rodriguez called it an historic step "to recover such an essential service." Rodriguez, in power since the United States ousted Nicolas Maduro in January, first held talks with General Electric in April.

The deal with General Electric was struck under the leadership of Energy Minister Rolando Alcalá, an electrical engineer appointed to the job by Rodríguez three months ago. His appointment was seen as a welcome change after six years in which the ministry was headed by senior members of the military, who failed to fix the failing grid. Rodríguez has closely co-operated with the Trump administration on a number of matters. Last week, US forces carried out a military strike in which the leader of the Tren de Aragua criminal gang was killed. US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth said that the operation had been carried out "in full co-operation with Venezuelan security forces", something which would have been unthinkable when Maduro was in power. However, members of Venezuela's opposition have pointed out that there have been very few change ---

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Venezuela's interim president has signed an agreement with US energy giant General Electric to rebuild the country's electricity grid.

Delcy Rodríguez, who was sworn in shortly after US forces seized Venezuela's leader, Nicolás Maduro, in January, announced the move at a televised event at the presidential palace on Monday.

The agreement is the latest sign that the interim leader - who was a fierce critic of the US before Maduro's ouster - is opening up Venezuela's economy to US investors and companies.

Critics of her government have warned that while Rodríguez appears to be loosening the state's control over the economy, many key institutions remain firmly under her party's control.

Venezuela suffers from frequent power cuts and its power system - which was nationalised in 2007 under Maduro's mentor, Hugo Chávez - is in dire need of repair and investment.

Rodríguez described the signing of the agreement with General Electric Vernova, the US company's local branch, as "a historic step for Venezuela", which would allow the South American nation to restore what she called "an essential service".

Power cuts often last 10 hours or longer and have affected major cities, including the capital, Caracas.

The Maduro government had blamed a drought for the frequent outages, which meant that the Guri hydroelectric power dam - a key source of electricity - was not producing enough energy to meet demand.

But analysts have long warned that a lack of investment in and maintenance of the power grid, coupled with high consumption, have created an energy crisis which has been one of the blocks to Venezuela's economic recovery.

The deal with General Electric was struck under the leadership of Energy Minister Rolando Alcalá, an electrical engineer appointed to the job by Rodríguez three months ago.

His appointment was seen as a welcome change after six years in which the ministry was headed by senior members of the military, who failed to fix the failing grid.

Rodríguez has closely co-operated with the Trump administration on a number of matters.

Last week, US forces carried out a military strike in which the leader of the Tren de Aragua criminal gang was killed.

US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth said that the operation had been carried out "in full co-operation with Venezuelan security forces", something which would have been unthinkable when Maduro was in power.

However, members of Venezuela's opposition have pointed out that there have been very few change

---

[Lähde: Le Monde]
Venezuela signed an agreement on Monday, June 15, with General Electric for the US utility giant to rebuild its decrepit power grid, the South American country's interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, said. Most of Venezuela, including the capital Caracas, endures daily blackouts lasting up to 10 hours as the country deals with decades of neglect and underinvestment in the energy sector and elsewhere.

Speaking alongside GE executives at the presidential palace, Rodriguez called it an historic step "to recover such an essential service." Rodriguez, in power since the United States ousted Nicolas Maduro in January, first held talks with General Electric in April.

The discussions came as her government was under pressure from President Donald Trump to open Venezuela's oil-rich economy and resources to American companies. Much of Venezuela's infrastructure is in a bad state after 13 years of rule under Maduro, who blamed the country's decline on US sanctions.

Venezuela now consumes about 16% more electricity than it generates, which is about 12,000 megawatts per day, according to opposition lawmaker Ezio Angelini. The electrical grid was nationalized in 2007 by then-president Hugo Chavez, a socialist icon.

Rodriguez said at the presidential palace that the goal of the new contract with GE is to increase electricity output by 1,000 megawatts per day in the first two years and by 5,000 megawatts in four years.

payload.title: Venezuela sopi General Electricin kanssa sähköverkon korjaamisesta
payload.summary: Venezuelan väliaikainen presidentti Delcy Rodríguez on ilmoittanut sopimuksesta General Electricin kanssa maan rapautuneen sähköverkon uudistamiseksi. Sopimus kertoo myös Yhdysvaltain yritysten ja Venezuelan väliaikaishallinnon lähentyneestä yhteistyöstä.
payload.content:
Venezuelan väliaikainen presidentti Delcy Rodríguez on allekirjoittanut yhdysvaltalaisen General Electricin kanssa sopimuksen maan sähköverkon jälleenrakentamisesta. Maan sähköjärjestelmä on kärsinyt pitkään laiminlyönneistä ja alinvestoinneista, ja suuri osa Venezuelasta, pääkaupunki Caracas mukaan lukien, kokee lähteiden mukaan päivittäin jopa kymmenen tunnin sähkökatkoja.

## Sopimus julkistettiin presidentinpalatsissa

Rodríguez ilmoitti sopimuksesta maanantaina televisioidussa tilaisuudessa presidentinpalatsissa. Tilaisuudessa oli mukana General Electricin johtoa. Rodríguez kuvasi järjestelyä historialliseksi askeleeksi välttämättömän palvelun palauttamisessa.

Sopimus koskee Venezuelan heikossa kunnossa olevan sähköverkon korjaamista ja uudistamista. Maan sähköjärjestelmä kansallistettiin vuonna 2007 Hugo Chávezin aikana. Sen jälkeen energia-ala on kärsinyt vuosien laiminlyönneistä ja puutteellisista investoinneista.

General Electricin kanssa tehty järjestely on valmisteltu energiaministeri Rolando Alcalán johdolla. Alcalá on sähköinsinööri, jonka Rodríguez nimitti tehtävään kolme kuukautta sitten. Nimitys nähtiin muutoksena edeltäneeseen kuuden vuoden jaksoon, jolloin ministeriötä johtivat korkea-arvoiset sotilastaustaiset henkilöt, eikä sähköverkon ongelmia saatu ratkaistua.

## Yhteistyö Yhdysvaltain kanssa on tiivistynyt

Sopimus on uusi merkki siitä, että Venezuelan väliaikaishallinto avaa maan taloutta yhdysvaltalaisille sijoittajille ja yrityksille. Rodríguez nousi valtaan sen jälkeen, kun Yhdysvaltain joukot syrjäyttivät Nicolás Maduron tammikuussa. Hän oli aiemmin jyrkkä Yhdysvaltain arvostelija, mutta on sittemmin tehnyt tiivistä yhteistyötä Trumpin hallinnon kanssa useissa kysymyksissä.

Rodríguezin ja General Electricin ensimmäiset keskustelut käytiin lähteiden mukaan huhtikuussa. Nyt solmittu sopimus on osa laajempaa muutosta, jossa väliaikaishallinto hakee yhteistyötä yhdysvaltalaisten yritysten kanssa maan keskeisten palvelujen korjaamiseksi.

## Arvostelijat varoittavat vallan keskittymisestä

Yhteistyö on näkynyt myös turvallisuuskysymyksissä. Viime viikolla Yhdysvaltain joukot tekivät sotilaallisen iskun, jossa Tren de Aragua -rikollisryhmän johtaja kuoli. Yhdysvaltain puolustusministeri Pete Hegsethin mukaan operaatio toteutettiin täydessä yhteistyössä Venezuelan turvallisuusjoukkojen kanssa.

Rodríguezin hallintoa arvostelevat tahot ovat kuitenkin varoittaneet, että vaikka valtio näyttää höllentävän otettaan taloudesta, monet keskeiset instituutiot ovat yhä hänen puolueensa hallinnassa. Opposition mukaan todelliset muutokset ovat jääneet vähäisiksi.
summary_bullets: Venezuela on sopinut General Electricin kanssa maan sähköverkon jälleenrakentamisesta.
Maa kärsii laajoista ja päivittäisistä sähkökatkoista vuosien alinvestointien jälkeen.
Sopimus kuvaa Venezuelan väliaikaishallinnon tiivistyvää yhteistyötä yhdysvaltalaisten yritysten kanssa.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu annettuihin lähdekatkelmiin. Taustatiedot Maduron syrjäyttämisestä ja Yhdysvaltain toimista on käsitelty lähteiden väitteinä ilman lisälaajennuksia.
